head.h1: Vegetarian Catering in Dubai — What It Costs and How to Book

opening_paragraph: Vegetarian catering in Dubai starts from AED 90 per person for buffet formats, and from AED 700 with a myCHEF chef cooking on site. Both cover a fully meat-free spread built around your guests — menu design, cooking, service staff, plating and cleanup. It is not a side salad next to the "real" food: it is the whole event, drawn from Indian, Mediterranean and Italian kitchens so plant-based guests are catered to properly. Share your date, guest count and venue and a vetted vegetarian caterer in Dubai returns an itemised proposal, usually inside one business day.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What vegetarian catering in Dubai includes
new_paragraphs: It includes the full run of the event, not just the cooking. A vegetarian catering company in Dubai should hand you one team that owns every step: a menu designed to your brief and a tasting to sign it off; a private vegetarian chef cooking fresh on site instead of reheating trays; front-of-house service staff where the format needs them; plating and presentation; and complete setup and cleanup so you host, not cook. Because the whole menu is meat-free by design, there is no token vegetarian option bolted on at the end, so every dish on the table is one your guests can eat. Allergen cross-contact is a separate question, and it is reviewed with the assigned culinary partner for each individual booking, not assumed away. Vegetarian catering services in Dubai from myCHEF also cover the practical layer: portioning for real appetites, allergen labelling on request, and clear timing so hot food lands hot. You get a single point of contact from first message to final plate cleared.

add_block.new_heading: Is vegetarian food available in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Yes, and widely. Dubai is an easy city to eat vegetarian in: Indian, Levantine and Mediterranean cooking are everywhere here, and all three carry deep meat-free traditions — a Gujarati thali, a mezze table of hummus, moutabel and tabbouleh, a South Indian dosa counter. Supermarkets stock vegetarian and vegan ranges as standard, and restaurants across the city list meat-free sections instead of one token dish. Catering is where the question gets sharper. It is not whether vegetarian food is available in Dubai, but whether a caterer will build the whole menu meat-free instead of setting one tray of vegetables beside the meat. That is what myCHEF arranges: a chaat counter, a Jain module cooked without onion or garlic, plated Continental mains, and nothing on the table your guests cannot eat.

new_paragraphs: The same meat-free kitchen scales cleanly from an intimate dinner to a 200-guest reception. Vegetarian catering for events in Dubai suits Hindu and Jain family weddings where the whole guest list eats vegetarian, mixed-diet celebrations where you want plant-based to be the generous default, and festival occasions like Diwali or Navratri. For the boardroom, corporate vegetarian catering in Dubai keeps working lunches, launches and away-days inclusive without anyone feeling short-changed, and a growing number of Dubai companies now brief vegetarian-first. Vegetarian party catering in Dubai handles birthdays, baby showers and villa gatherings with grazing tables, live stations and canapés that happen to be meatless. Whatever the occasion, the menu is engineered so vegetarian food catering in Dubai reads as abundance, not restriction.

add_block.new_heading: The vegetarian, vegan and Jain menu in full
new_paragraphs: Here is the working repertoire, in the order it reaches the table. Guests who normally fall back on vegetarian restaurants in Dubai for range get the same breadth at their own venue. Pick the lines you want and the menu is composed around them — a pure-vegetarian wedding, a plant-based corporate lunch, a Jain thali service, or a mixed-diet party where the meat-free table is the main event, not the accommodation.
Welcome drinks
One drink opens the service and is included in every package tier.
Kesariya Lassi: saffron-scented sweet yoghurt drink.
Mango Lassi: ripe mango blended thick with yoghurt.
Govinda’s Thandai: chilled milk with almonds, fennel and cardamom.
Buttermilk, chaas: salted, cumin-spiked, served cold.
Classic Lemonade: fresh lemon, mint and sugar.
Fresh Juices and Smoothies: seasonal fruit, pressed on the day.
Rabri Faluda: reduced milk, vermicelli, basil seeds and rose — a top-tier line.
Cold mezze — naturally vegan
The Arabic opening spread carries a plant-based table without a single substitution, and each line is tagged, not lumped under a footnote. Six to ten items make the course.
Hommos (vegan): chickpeas, tahina, lemon and olive oil.
Moutabal (vegan): smoked aubergine whipped with tahina.
Baba Ghanouj (vegan): chopped grilled aubergine with tomato, pepper and pomegranate molasses.
Fattoush (vegan): garden salad with sumac and crisp bread.
Tabbouleh (vegan): parsley-led, with bulgur, tomato and lemon.
Stuffed Vine Leaves (vegan): rice and herbs rolled cold, finished with lemon.
Muhammara: roasted red pepper and walnut dip.
Eggplant Salad (vegan): grilled aubergine dressed with garlic and lemon.
Crudité (vegan): cucumber, tomato, radish and carrot, cut to order.
Grazing-table extensions: olives, labneh, Arabic bread and kaak sticks.
Plant-forward salads
Three to five, so a vegan guest reads the main menu instead of a short separate one.
Quinoa Salad (vegan): quinoa with herbs, cucumber and a lemon dressing.
Kale Salad with Walnuts, Mango and Strawberry (vegan): massaged kale, toasted walnuts, fruit.
Baby Spinach with Pomegranate (vegan): spinach leaves, pomegranate seeds, citrus dressing.
Beetroot Salad with Sweet Corn (vegan): roasted beetroot against sweet corn.
Lentil Salad (vegan): brown lentils with red onion and parsley.
Three Beans Salad (vegan): kidney, chickpea and green beans in vinaigrette.
Rajma Salad (vegan): spiced red kidney beans with onion and coriander.
Aloo Chana Chat Salad (vegan): potato and chickpea tossed with chaat masala.
Indian Summer Salad (vegan): cucumber, tomato, onion, lemon and green chilli.

Soups
One on a buffet, chosen from five.
Coriander Lemon: clear broth finished with coriander and lemon.
Sweet Corn: thickened corn soup with diced vegetables.
Cream of Tomato: roasted tomato, cream and basil.
Clear Vegetable: light broth with julienned vegetables.

Cold canapés
Six to eight varieties for a standing reception.
Canapé Chaat in Taco Cups (vegan): the chaat build in a crisp taco cup.
Hummus Beetroot in Tartlet (vegan): beetroot hummus in a pastry shell.

Vine Leaves Tzatziki in Shooters (vegan): a rolled vine leaf standing in a herbed dip.

Buffalo Mozzarella with Cherry Tomato and Pesto in Shots: the caprese idea, served upright.
Roast Tomato Caprese with Basil: slow-roast tomato, basil and soft cheese.
Tomato, Mozzarella and Basil Bruschetta: cut and topped on site.

Four to six of these go on a menu, and they are the tray guests remember.

Live stations
A wedding takes three to five, a corporate lunch one or two, and the contents are spelled out, not left as “live cooking&rdquo.

Stations carry the longest lead time of any format, because the equipment and the station chefs both have to be confirmed with the partner before the date is held. Where each one can stand is worth settling in the same conversation. The live tandoor is an outdoor, ground-level machine: villa gardens, driveways and permitted outdoor events take it, while a villa's indoor kitchen, an apartment balcony and a yacht do not — there the paneer tikka and the breads are fired in the licensed tandoor kitchen and finished hot at the counter, brushed and served in front of guests. The saj is the easy one: gas outdoors at a villa, electric wherever the power carries it including indoors and on a terrace, and only on a boat does it come off, where no catering gas cylinder may be brought aboard and the breads are baked ashore then filled and rolled to order on deck. Live frying is the strict one. Hot oil wants extraction and suppression that no apartment kitchen or balcony has, so pakora, samosa, falafel, tempura and luqaimat are fried in the licensed kitchen, carried hot and crisped to order on site, with the luqaimat syrup poured at the station so the counter still reads as live. On a rooftop or at a desert camp myCHEF confirms all three with the building management or the site operator before quoting.

Eggless sits apart from vegan on purpose — the Indian-vegetarian guest and the vegan guest are asking two different questions, and answering only one of them shows.
Dietary notes, minimums and lead times

Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event. Jain, sattvic and no-onion-no-garlic briefs are built as their own menu and are confirmed with the partner the same way.

Volume formats start at 10 guests and buffets at 20, with a minimum order value of AED 900; the staffed private-chef format carries no minimum headcount. On timing: we recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. Need a vegetarian sooner than the usual lead time? The answer depends on the date, so ask before ruling it out.

add_block.new_heading: Service styles, dietary needs and logistics
